chunks: A servant wrote to Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: I have come across a group of Muslims who are heretics and a group of Christians who are also heretics.

He said: As for those who were from the Muslims, born upon the natural disposition, then apostatized, strike their neck and do not seek their repentance. And as for those who were not born among them upon the natural disposition, seek their repentance. If they repent, [leave them]; otherwise, strike their neck. And as for the Christians, what they are upon is greater than heresy.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: The natural disposition (innate inclination towards monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling for executing a Muslim apostate based on whether they were born into Islam or not?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Imam Ali’s nuanced approach to apostasy by distinguishing between those born into the natural disposition (*fitrah*) of Islam, who are executed immediately without seeking repentance (*istitabah*), and those who embraced Islam later, who are given a chance to repent. The ruling also extends to Christians, whose belief system is deemed graver than heresy (*zanadiqa*), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view on the severity of deviating from the innate monotheistic truth. This distinction underscores the importance of *fitrah* in determining the legal status of an apostate within Shia fiqh.
